coreIdea: Cut property: min edge crossing any cut is in SOME MST. Cycle property: max edge in any cycle is excluded (unless it's a bridge). Distinct weights → unique MST.
mustRememberFormulas: Kruskal's: O(E log E) (or O(E) if pre-sorted). Prim's: O(E log V) heap, O(V²) array
Global minimum edge is ALWAYS in every MST
Uniform weight +c: MST set unchanged, new total = old + (n-1)c
Non-linear transform (e.g. squaring): MST set NOT guaranteed unchanged

commonTrapsQuickList: Max-weight edge is NOT always excluded — bridges must stay regardless of weight
Only the GLOBAL minimum edge is guaranteed in every MST — second-smallest is not
Distinct weights → MST is unique; repeated weights → possibly multiple MSTs (count ties)
Linear weight transforms (+c, ×c) preserve MST set; non-linear (squaring) don't guarantee it
highYieldPyqLessons: Direct MST computation (15/35) is the bread-and-butter skill — get fast and error-free at Kruskal's with cycle-checking.
Theoretical property claims (8/35) reward knowing cut/cycle property as PROOFS, not just facts — you can construct counterexamples on the fly for FALSE claims.
